owner_creation.analysis: FILE:src/xbuf.rs: xbuffer owns data plus end/size/init_size metadata; init starts empty and add_byte acquires ecalloc storage when capacity is exhausted.
owner_creation.invariant: A live xbuffer needs one coherent allocation descriptor.

aliases_escapes.analysis: FILE:src/xbuf.rs: xbuf_char_data returns a raw borrowed pointer, while Copy/Clone can duplicate the owning descriptor; add_data retains its source pointer across calls that may grow the destination.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Raw aliases must be retired before buffer growth.
limitations: This review records source-level raw owner, self-alias and commit-order hazards; no new runtime reproduction or product fix is claimed.

callback_targets.analysis: FILE:src/xbuf.rs: Calls are direct ecalloc/memcpy/free and an optional fault hook; there is no registered callback that can extend a slice lifetime.

invalidation.analysis: FILE:src/xbuf.rs: Growth frees old data at 73; a source pointer into that same allocation in add_data can then be stale on the next loop iteration.

mutation_commit.analysis: FILE:src/xbuf.rs: size is assigned before overflow handling and allocation, and set resets dst before copying src; these are not failure-preserving staged updates.

release_pair.analysis: FILE:src/xbuf.rs: deinit pairs ecalloc with free and resets fields, but copied descriptors or repeated initialization of a live owner can invalidate that single-release contract.
